import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source_0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_0.csv"
source_1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_1.csv"
source_2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_2.csv"
source_3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_3.csv"
source_4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_4.csv"
source_5_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_5.csv"
source_6_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_6.csv"
source_7_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_7.csv"
source_8_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_8.csv"
source_9_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_9.csv"

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_0_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'total_crime', 'violation', 'misdemeanor', 'felony']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_1_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_2_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'indicator', 'counts']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_3_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_4_path, index_col=0)  # ['boro', 'zipcode']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_5_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'theft', 'assault', 'harassment']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_6_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'counts']
df7 = pd.read_csv(source_7_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']
df8 = pd.read_csv(source_8_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'counts']
df9 = pd.read_csv(source_9_path, index_col=0)  # ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts']

# --- Transformation Plan ---
# Target schema:
# ['zipcode': int,
#  'businesses_x': str, 'counts_x': int,
#  'businesses_y': str, 'counts_y': int,
#  'businesses_x_5': str, 'counts_x_6': int,
#  'businesses_y_7': str, 'counts_y_8': int,
#  'boro': str,
#  'counts_x_10': int, 'counts_y_11': int,
#  'indicator': str,
#  'counts': int,
#  'total_crime': int,
#  'violation': int,
#  'misdemeanor': int,
#  'felony': int,
#  'theft': int,
#  'assault': int,
#  'harassment': int]

# Observations:
# - df1, df3, df7, df9 have the same schema ['zipcode', 'businesses', 'counts'].
#   The target table has 4 pairs of businesses/counts columns with suffixes:
#   (businesses_x, counts_x), (businesses_y, counts_y), (businesses_x_5, counts_x_6), (businesses_y_7, counts_y_8)
#   This suggests these 4 source tables correspond to these 4 pairs.
#   We must assign each source table to one pair and rename columns accordingly.
#   From target examples and source examples:
#     - businesses_x, counts_x  ~ Sidewalk Cafe (df9)
#     - businesses_y, counts_y  ~ Pawnbroker (df1)
#     - businesses_x_5, counts_x_6 ~ Debt Collection Agency (df3)
#     - businesses_y_7, counts_y_8 ~ Cigarette Retail Dealer (df7)
#
# - df4 has ['boro', 'zipcode'] - dimension table for borough info.
# - df0 has crime stats: ['zipcode', 'total_crime', 'violation', 'misdemeanor', 'felony']
# - df5 has ['zipcode', 'theft', 'assault', 'harassment']
# - df2 has ['zipcode', 'indicator', 'counts'] - indicator and counts columns
# - df6 and df8 have ['zipcode', 'counts'] but target has two counts columns named counts_x_10 and counts_y_11.
#   We will assign df6 to counts_x_10 and df8 to counts_y_11 based on naming pattern.
#
# - The target column 'counts' corresponds to df2.counts (indicator counts).
#
# Join all on 'zipcode' (and 'boro' from df4).
# The businesses/counts columns come from the 4 business-related dfs renamed accordingly.
# The rest are numeric columns from crime and counts dfs.
#
# Steps:
# 1. Rename df1, df3, df7, df9 columns to match target business/count columns.
# 2. Merge all business dfs on 'zipcode' with outer join to keep all zipcodes.
# 3. Merge with df4 on 'zipcode' to get 'boro'.
# 4. Merge with df0 (crime stats).
# 5. Merge with df5 (theft, assault, harassment).
# 6. Merge with df2 (indicator, counts).
# 7. Merge with df6 and df8 for counts_x_10 and counts_y_11.
# 8. Fill missing values for counts with 0 and for strings with empty string.
# 9. Cast columns to correct types.
# 10. Reorder columns to match target schema.
#
# Note: We use outer joins to preserve all zipcodes appearing in any source.

# Rename business dfs columns to target names
df9_renamed = df9.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_x',
    'counts': 'counts_x'
})  # Sidewalk Cafe

df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_y',
    'counts': 'counts_y'
})  # Pawnbroker

df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_x_5',
    'counts': 'counts_x_6'
})  # Debt Collection Agency

df7_renamed = df7.rename(columns={
    'businesses': 'businesses_y_7',
    'counts': 'counts_y_8'
})  # Cigarette Retail Dealer

# Merge all business dfs on 'zipcode'
df_business = df9_renamed.merge(df1_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer') \
                         .merge(df3_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer') \
                         .merge(df7_renamed, on='zipcode', how='outer')

# Merge with borough info (df4)
df_boro = df_business.merge(df4, on='zipcode', how='left')

# Merge with crime stats (df0)
df_crime = df_boro.merge(df0, on='zipcode', how='left')

# Merge with theft, assault, harassment (df5)
df_crime2 = df_crime.merge(df5, on='zipcode', how='left')

# Merge with indicator and counts (df2)
df_indicator = df_crime2.merge(df2, on='zipcode', how='left')

# Merge with counts_x_10 (df6) and counts_y_11 (df8)
df_counts_x_10 = df_indicator.merge(df6.rename(columns={'counts': 'counts_x_10'}), on='zipcode', how='left')
df_counts_y_11 = df_counts_x_10.merge(df8.rename(columns={'counts': 'counts_y_11'}), on='zipcode', how='left')

# Fill missing string columns with empty string and numeric columns with 0
string_cols = ['businesses_x', 'businesses_y', 'businesses_x_5', 'businesses_y_7', 'boro', 'indicator']
for col in string_cols:
    if col in df_counts_y_11.columns:
        df_counts_y_11[col] = df_counts_y_11[col].fillna('')

# Numeric columns to fill with 0
numeric_cols = [
    'counts_x', 'counts_y', 'counts_x_6', 'counts_y_8',
    'counts_x_10', 'counts_y_11', 'counts',
    'total_crime', 'violation', 'misdemeanor', 'felony',
    'theft', 'assault', 'harassment'
]
for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in df_counts_y_11.columns:
        df_counts_y_11[col] = df_counts_y_11[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'zipcode',
    'businesses_x', 'counts_x',
    'businesses_y', 'counts_y',
    'businesses_x_5', 'counts_x_6',
    'businesses_y_7', 'counts_y_8',
    'boro',
    'counts_x_10', 'counts_y_11',
    'indicator',
    'counts',
    'total_crime',
    'violation',
    'misdemeanor',
    'felony',
    'theft',
    'assault',
    'harassment'
]

# Select only target columns (some zipcodes may be missing some columns if source missing)
df_final = df_counts_y_11[target_columns]

# Save to CSV
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

# Source7: businesses, counts -> businesses_y_7, counts_y_8

# Join Source1 and Source3 on zipcode
result = pd.merge(source1, source3, on="zipcode", how="inner")

result = pd.merge(result, source9, on="zipcode", how="inner")
